body:
CROSSED AGAIN - my #2049 round-2 verdict went out just before this and reports the allowlist gap from the other end. I found it by reading the rework diff; product found it by running the chain. Same defect, two independent routes, and the interesting part is that NEITHER route was the static verification all three of us did.

I OWN MY THIRD OF IT AND IT IS ALREADY IN THE VERDICT. In round 1 I traced CronJobFailed to events.rs:291, maintenance_schedule.rs:1615 and watch.rs:470, wrote that the chain "exists statically", and separately quoted the init_cmd.rs scaffold hunk containing the command string - and never asked whether that string was allowlisted. I verified the link AFTER the gap and had the link BEFORE it on screen. Drawing the static-existence line and then not applying it to the link I was actually looking at is worse than not drawing it.

I TESTED BUG-1557'S PREMISE, because "today's five pass only because of who wrote them" is checkable and the answer changes its urgency.

    scaffolded command= strings, init_cmd.rs   cache verify, doctor, notify check,
                                               queue gc, session reap
    valid_commands()                           the same five, plus fetch --code-only,
                                               store compact, store gc

ALL FIVE ARE ALLOWLISTED TODAY. So BUG-1557 is a structural risk and not a present breakage - nothing on main ships a dead job right now. That is worth having on the spec because it separates "fix before the next scaffold change" from "something is broken in the field", and I would rather you had it from a check than from my assuming the worse case.

ONE TRAP FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS IT, and it would bite immediately. The relationship is NOT set equality. The allowlist has eight entries and scaffolding uses five; fetch --code-only, store compact and store gc are allowlisted with no scaffolded example, which is fine. A check asserting the two sets match fails on day one for three false reasons and gets weakened or deleted. THE ONE-DIRECTIONAL FORM IS THE CORRECT ONE: every scaffolded `command =` must parse. The converse is not a defect.

There is also a sixth `command =` in that file at init_cmd.rs:2177 - the literal placeholder "<allow-listed aida subcommand>" in documentation text. A naive extractor picks it up and it will never parse. Either scope the check to the schedule.jobs block or exclude the documentation example deliberately, but do it knowingly rather than discovering it as a failure.

SCOPING MY OWN CHECK: I grepped init_cmd.rs only, for `command *= *"`, six matches, one of them the placeholder above. Scaffolded jobs defined anywhere else, or written with a different key, would not have matched.

ON YOUR HYPOTHESIS-FIT LINE - "how well a hypothesis fits is not evidence for it, it is a measure of how much you will regret not checking it" is sharper than what I sent you and I would keep your wording over mine.

ON THE NULL-GREP ENTRY - product reporting their own near-miss is the right instinct and the pairing is what makes it teachable: ScheduledJobFailed was an invented NAME where grep's silence was true and saved them; on_events/matches_on/trigger_events were invented SEARCH TERMS where grep's silence was meaningless. Same tool, same empty output, opposite value, nothing in the output telling them apart. "A null grep is evidence about the code only if the pattern came FROM the code" is the right rule, and the operational form is: before trusting an empty result, find one case where the pattern DOES match something you already know exists.

MY NON-BLOCKING FINDING IS SUBSUMED BY YOURS AND YOURS IS BETTER. I flagged that the new allowlist entry has no test. BUG-1557's generated check covers the class; mine covered the instance. That is the half-fix shape I have been asking others to avoid all night - I named the cited site instead of the seam, on the same PR where I had asked the author to do the opposite about the median comments. Please treat mine as closed by yours.

VERDICT STANDS AS RECORDED: #2049 APPROVED at cd21a1dc0a9e for this PR's MECHANISM only, explicitly not spec closure. Criteria 2-zero-half, 7 and enablement are yours and open. Not mergeable regardless: three Builds pending and the merge-hold label present.

Board: 13 open, 13 with a recorded sha, 0 moved. #2033 held.
subject: BUG-1557 premise tested: all five scaffolded commands ARE allowlisted today, so structural risk not present breakage - plus the set-equality trap and the doc placeholder that will bite the implementer
